summary: This study evaluates the utility of optical coherence tomography (OCT) in patients with chiasmal compression from para-chiasmal lesions, specifically examining its role in predicting visual field outcomes post-operatively. A meta-analysis of 97 studies involving 5,300 patient eyes and 2,209 controls found significantly thinner peripapillary retinal nerve fiber layer, macular RNFL, macular ganglion cell complex, and macular ganglion cell–inner plexiform layer in patients compared to controls. The results suggest that OCT may support diagnosis and prognosis for patients with para-chiasmal lesions, particularly in patients with good visual recovery, who had higher pre-operative mean peripapillary RNFL thickness.
